title: A 4 GB Laptop GPU Beats a 12-Core CPU by 4.3x on Gemma 4
why_read: A concrete, methodologically careful micro-benchmark comparing CPU versus a low-end GPU for running a small language model gives a useful practical data point for local LLM deployment decisions.
analysis: This post benchmarks running the Gemma model (quantized to q4_0) via llama.cpp on the same laptop in two configurations, CPU-only versus using an old, low-VRAM GTX 1650 Ti GPU, changing only a single command-line flag. It reports the GPU wins decode speed by 4.3x while using under 1.6GB of VRAM, which is a useful data point for people wondering whether even old/weak GPUs are worth using for small local LLM inference. The methodology, keeping everything else byte-identical and varying only the offload flag, is commendably rigorous for a blog-level benchmark. It's a narrow, single-machine result rather than a broad study, but the specificity and reproducibility give it modest practical value.
